lines.speaker: Ms. Hạnh (Interviewer)
lines.text: Can you tell me about a project you're really proud of?

lines.speaker: Long (Candidate)
lines.text: Sure. Last year, I spearheaded a project to replace our legacy system for managing orders.

lines.speaker: Ms. Hạnh (Interviewer)
lines.text: What was the problem with the old system?

lines.speaker: Long (Candidate)
lines.text: It was very slow. During sales events, it could take one minute to confirm an order, and customers complained a lot.

lines.speaker: Long (Candidate)
lines.text: First, I found the bottleneck. It was the way we saved data. Then my team of four built a new service and migrated all the data step by step.

lines.speaker: Ms. Hạnh (Interviewer)
lines.text: Moving data can be risky. How did you avoid problems?

lines.speaker: Long (Candidate)
lines.text: We ran both systems at the same time for two weeks and compared the results every day. We also asked end users to test it early.

lines.speaker: Long (Candidate)
lines.text: We launched on time, and it resulted in orders being confirmed in under three seconds. Complaints dropped by about seventy percent.

questions.q: What was the main problem with the old system?
options: It was too slow to confirm orders
Nobody knew how to use it

questions.q: How did Long's team reduce the risk of moving data?
options: They ran both systems together and compared results
They moved all the data in one night
Complaints dropped by about seventy percent

shadowing: Last year, I spearheaded a project to replace our slow legacy order system.
The situation was difficult because customers waited one minute to confirm each order.
My task was to find the bottleneck and fix it without stopping daily sales.
We migrated the data step by step and tested it with real end users.
As a result, we launched on time and complaints dropped by seventy percent.
